articles.headline: Six Popular Sugar Substitutes May Age Your Brain 1.6 Years Faster
articles.body: An eight-year study of nearly 13,000 adults reveals a striking link between high artificial sweetener consumption and accelerated cognitive decline. People who consumed the most sweeteners experienced a 62% faster drop in memory and thinking skills—equivalent to roughly 1.6 extra years of brain aging. The effect was strongest in adults under 60 and those with diabetes. Six specific sweeteners were flagged: aspartame, saccharin, acesulfame K, erythritol, sorbitol, and xylitol. Tagatose was the only one that showed no association. Researchers emphasize this is an observed link, not proof of direct causation, and further investigation is needed.
articles.takeaway: If you consume diet sodas or artificial sweeteners daily, consider cutting back—especially if you're under 60 or managing blood sugar.

articles.headline: Skip 42 Minutes of Sunlight Today, Boost Your Dementia Risk
articles.body: A sweeping study of 87,577 adults shows that getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily is a stronger predictor of dementia risk than six well-established factors like obesity and hearing loss. Researchers tracked wrist-worn light sensors over eight years and found that daytime exposure above 1,000 lux reduced dementia risk by 16%. Those getting the brightest light (5,000+ lux) saw even sharper risk reductions. The protective effect was strongest in people carrying the APOE-E4 gene and night owls. Nighttime light exposure made no difference. The finding doesn't prove sunlight prevents dementia, but it's a striking signal about light's role in brain health.
articles.takeaway: Aim for 42+ minutes of outdoor daylight daily. Your afternoon walk might be one of your most powerful preventive health moves.

articles.topic: PTSD treatment breakthrough with brain mapping
articles.headline: New Brain Stimulation Treatment Clears PTSD Symptoms in 68% of Patients
articles.body: A newly FDA-cleared treatment using personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation has achieved remarkable results for PTSD sufferers. Clinical trials showed a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission in patients who received the targeted therapy. Unlike medication-based approaches, this treatment uses brain imaging to identify abnormal activity patterns specific to each person, then delivers precise stimulation to reset those circuits. The breakthrough is significant because PTSD has historically resisted treatment in a substantial portion of patients. Researchers believe this precision approach could eventually transform treatment for other mental health conditions, offering hope for drug-free, long-term relief.
articles.takeaway: If standard PTSD treatments haven't worked, ask your provider about brain-targeted therapies—this technology just cleared FDA approval.

articles.headline: 30 Minutes in a Sauna Sends Your Immune Cells Into Active Patrol
articles.body: Finnish researchers discovered that a single 30-minute sauna session—including a brief cold shower halfway through—temporarily floods your bloodstream with circulating white blood cells. The surge resembles the immune mobilization that happens during intense exercise. Here's the catch: the body isn't making new immune cells; it's moving existing ones from tissues into circulation, where they can actively patrol for threats. The effect is temporary, and the study didn't measure long-term immunity benefits. But the finding offers a biological explanation for why regular sauna users report feeling better. Think of it as putting your immune system on higher alert mode, at least temporarily.
articles.takeaway: A regular sauna habit may give your immune system periodic wake-up calls, but it's not a substitute for sleep, nutrition, and exercise.

workout.title: Short Stride Acceleration: 30/30 Intro to Speed
workout.tip: Focus on smooth arm drive and controlled breathing during the 30-second push—don't sprint all-out. Your recovery jog should feel easy; if you can't talk, you're recovering too hard.
workout.warmup: 5 min: easy jog at conversational pace, then 6 x 20m strides with 40m walk recovery between each (stride should feel controlled, not maximal—build into it)

exercises.name: 30/30 Interval Block
exercises.notes: Run at a pace you could sustain for about 3-4 minutes (roughly 85–90% max effort). Keep your head still, shoulders relaxed, and cadence quick. Recovery jog should feel genuinely easy—this teaches your body pacing discipline.

workout.cooldown: 3 min easy jog, then 2 min stationary walk. Standing quad stretch 20 sec each leg, standing hamstring reach 20 sec each leg, open hip stretch 15 sec each side.
workout.description: Your first exposure to running speed work using safe, short 30-second efforts followed by 30-second recovery jogs. This session teaches your nervous system to move faster without the injury risk of longer intervals, making it perfect for 5K and 10K beginners building speed foundations.

meal.title: Peanut Butter Banana Toast with Milk
meal.description: Whole-wheat toast with peanut butter, banana and a drizzle of honey, plus a glass of milk. A classic pre-run breakfast.
meal.instructions: 1. Toast the bread. 2. Spread with peanut butter, top with banana and drizzle with honey. 3. Serve with the milk.
